bounded_statement: The report's sole selected result labels 0.3750 (37.50%) as the white-light flare occurrence rate 'for the complete planned set of 40 target stars,' but that value is computed as 12 flaring stars divided by the 32 retained (post-screening) stars. The retained-subset rate is presented as the rate for the complete planned domain of 40 stars, whose actual events-per-planned-unit value from the same data would be 12/40 = 0.3000. This mismatch is confined to the selected result's claimed domain; the accounting counts themselves (40 planned, 32 retained, 8 removed, 12 events) are internally consistent with the input data.

counterevidence_considered.description: Strongest counterevidence considered: the selected-result line transparently discloses its computation ('12 flaring stars / 32 exposure units'), and the accounting section separately reports 32 retained and 8 removed, so a careful reader could reconstruct the true retained-subset scope. This mitigates concealment but does not change the fact that the number 0.3750 is asserted as the occurrence rate for the complete planned set of 40 stars, which it is not.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: denominator of 32 disclosed within the claim itself

evidence.description: Independent recount of inputs/data.csv confirms the screening arithmetic: 8 of 40 stars fail the prespecified rule (coverage < 0.90: TIC-004, TIC-009, TIC-013, TIC-022, TIC-027, TIC-036; saturation_flag = 1: TIC-017, TIC-031, TIC-036), leaving 32 retained, of which 12 have flare_detected = yes; so 0.3750 can only arise from the retained-subset denominator.
The report itself records that no protocol amendment or approved deviation exists, ruling out an authorized redefinition of the target domain.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to defeat the demonstrated-issue verdict three ways. (1) Alternative reading: perhaps 'for the complete planned set' merely names the program rather than the rate's domain — but the Scientific target section states the rate 'is stated as applying to that complete planned set of 40 target stars,' which forecloses that reading. (2) Arithmetic: I recomputed from inputs/data.csv; 0.3750 matches only 12/32 (retained subset), while the complete-domain events-per-planned-unit value would be 12/40 = 0.3000, confirming the claimed value belongs to the subset. (3) Authorization: I looked for an amendment or deviation redefining the target to the retained subset; the report explicitly states none exists, and the task mandates the complete planned set. The transparency of the '/ 32 exposure units' disclosure is the only mitigating fact, and it makes the mismatch visible rather than resolving it. The verdict survives falsification.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py sets denominator = n_retained (the 32 screened-in stars) while build_report hard-codes the claim language to the complete planned set of `planned` (40) stars; the retained-subset denominator is therefore passed into a complete-domain claim, with no protocol amendment or approved deviation recorded that would authorize the substitution.
